audit.description: Changed production code in copydetect/detector.py replaces the source import `from jinja2 import Template` with the real target import `from mako.template import Template`, and the report template syntax in copydetect/data/report.html is converted to Mako directives and `${...}` expressions. Dynamic evidence shows a production import and Template attribute access from `mako.template` at copydetect/detector.py:19 with origin under site-packages/mako, while source import counts from repo and production code are zero. Static evidence reports no source imports, one target evidence file, and no target provider or local target spec, so the target use does not appear to be a fake shim.
evidence: copydetect/detector.py diff: `from jinja2 import Template` replaced by `from mako.template import Template`.
copydetect/data/report.html diff: Jinja loops/variables converted to Mako `% for` blocks and `${...}` expressions.
Dynamic metrics: target_import and target_attr_access for `mako.template.Template` from production file copydetect/detector.py, origin site-packages/mako/__init__.py.
Static anti-cheat: copydetect/detector.py imports_target=true, imports_source=false, fake_target_added_code=false, target_provider_added=false.
reasons: Production code imports and uses mako.template.Template.
Jinja2 import was removed from changed production code.
Dynamic audit observed real mako package use from site-packages.
No local fake target provider or target sys.modules alias was reported.
